messages.content: How far will a car travel in time 't' when launched with velocity 'v' at an angle 'theta'?

function.name: calculate_projectile_range
function.description: Calculate the range of a projectile launched at an angle with initial velocity, using the kinematic equation. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

initial_velocity.description: The initial velocity at which projectile is launched. This is a float type value.

angle.description: The angle at which projectile is launched. This should be in degrees. This is a float type value.

time.description: The time in seconds after which the range is to be calculated. This is a float type value.

message.reasoning:
The user asks: "How far will a car travel in time 't' when launched with velocity 'v' at an angle 'theta'?" They want distance traveled in time t given launch velocity v and angle theta. This is essentially projectile motion horizontal distance: x = v * cos(theta) * t. But they mention "calculate_projectile_range" function. That function calculates range given initial_velocity, angle, and optional time (default 0.5). But we need to compute distance traveled in time t. So we can call the function with time=t. But the function signature expects time optional default 0.5. We can pass time=t. So we need to call functions.calculate_projectile_range with initial_velocity=v, angle=theta, time=t. Then output the result.

We need to use the function. So we produce a function call.
